This miscellaneous appeal by appellant/ Insurance Company under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is arising out of the Award dated 30/06/2018 passed by First Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Morena (M.P.) (hereinafter it would be referred to as "the Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case Nos.400166/2011 and 400028/2013, whereby the Claims Tribunal awarded NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20664 2 MA-4489-2018 compensations in favour of claimants with a direction to owner, driver of offending vehicle and Insurance Company to pay compensation amount jointly and severally.
2.

sentences.text: Counsel for appellant/Insurance Company submitted that at the time of accident offending vehicle Jeep i.e. MP06-B-1353 was insured as private vehicle which was being driven as a taxi at the time of accident with the consent of owner of offending vehicle against the terms and conditions of the insurance policy, therefore, appellant is not liable to pay any compensation to the claimants.

It is further submitted that according to the FIR (Ex.D-2), deceased- Mahaveer was travelling in offending jeep as a passenger after giving fare charges but the Claims Tribunal without considering this aspect, has passed the impugned award.
Hence, it is prayed that impugned award be set-aside and the Insurance Company be exonerated from its liability.
4. On the other hand- learned counsel for the Claimants supported the impugned Award and prayed for rejection of appeal.

5. Heard counsel of both the parties and perused the record.
6.

According to the FIR (EX.D-2) where it is mentioned that the deceased was travelling in the offending jeep as a passenger after giving fare charges but the FIR was lodged by Nathilal (AW.3)
who stated in his chief examination that he was coming from Chintamanpura to Dimni by walking.

Ramveer who is acquainted with the driver of offending jeep, was going to Ambah met him near Police Station Dimni and said him that he can also sit in the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:20664 3 MA-4489-2018 offending jeep without giving any fare charges.

7. In the case of Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Premlata Shukla and Ors.
reported in 2007 AIR SCW 3591, Hon'ble Apex Court held that:-
''13.

reported in 2007 AIR SCW 3591

sentences.text: However, the factum of an accident could also be proved from the First Information Report.

It is also to be noted that once a part of the contents of the document is admitted in evidence, the party bringing the same on record cannot be permitted to turn round and contend that the other contents contained in the rest part thereof had not been proved.
Both the parties have relied thereupon.
It was marked as an Exhibit as both the parties intended to rely upon them.

14. Once a part of it is relied upon by both the parties, the learned Tribunal cannot be said to have committed any illegality in relying upon the other part, irrespective of the contents of the document been proved or not.

If the contents have been proved,
the question of reliance thereupon only upon a part thereof and not upon the rest, on the technical ground that the same had not been proved in accordance with law,
would not arise.
15. A party objecting to the admissibility of a document must raise its objection at the appropriate time.

If the objection is not raised and the document is allowed to be marked and that too at the instance of a party which had proved the same and wherefor consent of the other party has been obtained, the former in our opinion cannot be permitted to turn round and raise a contention that the contents of the National Insurance Company Ltd. sentences.text: (emphasis underlined)
8. On perusal of statement of Nathilal (A.W.3), it is found that Nathilal (A.W3) was an illiterate person and he put thumb impression on the FIR, therefore, he was unable to read out the FIR.
This witness in his cross- examination also deposed that the FIR was not read out to him.
He and other persons who sat in the offending jeep, did not give any fare charges to the driver of the offending jeep.

Under such circumstances, it is the duty of the Insurance NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20664 4 MA-4489-2018 Company to call the writer of FIR to prove the contents of FIR and prove the fact that the FIR was read out to Nathilal but in absence of non-examination of writer of FIR i.e. police authority, it can not be proved that the FIR was read out to Nathilal.
The evidence of Nathilal (A.W.3) was not rebutted by the Insurance Company, therefore, there is no reason to disbelieve the evidence of Nathilal.

9. O n the going through the evidence of Nathilal (AW-3), it is found that the deceased along with other persons was travelling in the offending jeep without giving any fare charges, which is not treated to be a taxi.

The Insurance Company was unable to prove that the owner and the driver of offending have breached the terms and conditions of insurance policy, therefore, the Claims Tribunal held that the owner and driver along-with Insurance Company are liable to pay compensation jointly and severally to the claimants.
Accordingly, no interference is warranted in the impugned award passed by the Claims Tribunal.
10. In view of foregoing discussion, the instant misc. appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.
